scope: Jan Sunwais, marches, protests, rallies, conventions and press conferences about the revision, organised by civil-society groups, independent commissions, youth groups and political parties of every side. Events organised by a political party are marked. The Election Commission's and the Chief Electoral Officers' own camps are left out, and their dates are on the Rules page.

events.title: Jan Sunwai on a public audit of the roll in Mangolpuri
events.organiser: Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan and Voter Adhikar Manch
events.place: Mangolpuri, New Delhi
events.quote: The findings were presented at a public hearing, or Jan Sunwai, held in Mangolpuri on September 5, 2026.
events.what: The findings of a door-to-door audit of Y Block were presented at a public hearing.

events.title: BJP press conference on the Election Commission and SIR row
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (national spokesperson Sambit Patra)
events.place: BJP Central Office, New Delhi
events.quote: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday defended the election commission over the row surrounding an alleged split among the poll panel's commissioners, with party MP Sambit Patra saying that internal deliberations between the three election commissioners were a sign of a healthy democracy.
events.what: BJP MP Sambit Patra held a press conference at which he defended the Election Commission after reports that two Election Commissioners had objected to decisions on the electoral rolls. He said the correspondence among the three commissioners was a sign of a healthy democracy.

events.title: Rahul Gandhi press conference on the Election Commissioners' objections to SIR decisions
events.organiser: Indian National Congress (Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi)
events.place: Congress headquarters, New Delhi
events.quote: Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi addresses the media on CEC Gyanesh Kumar row at the Congress Headquarters in New Delhi on September 24, 2026.
events.what: Rahul Gandhi held a press conference after a news report that two of the three Election Commissioners had formally objected at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions on the electoral rolls. He demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

events.title: Congress nationwide protests demanding the CEC's resignation
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, with state units, the Delhi Congress and the Indian Youth Congress
events.place: Several states, including marches in Patna, Lucknow, Assam (towards the Chief Electoral Officer's office), Jammu, Imphal and Delhi (Delhi Congress office towards Nirvachan Sadan)
events.quote: The Congress on Friday (September 25, 2026) led nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of compromising the integrity of India’s electoral process, with the party’s general secretary (organisation), K.C. Venugopal, seeking Mr. Kumar’s resignation and arrest for alleged electoral malpractice.
events.what: Congress workers held street protests in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police used water cannons in Patna, Lucknow and Punjab and detained protesters in Assam, Jammu, Odisha, Manipur, Delhi and other states.

events.title: Press conference of Voter Adhikar Manch
events.organiser: Voter Adhikar Manch
events.place: New Delhi
events.quote: Members of Voter Adhikar Manch addresses a press conference on SIR in New Delhi on September 28, 2026.
events.what: A press conference on the revision.

events.title: Jan Sunwai (public hearing) on wrongful SIR deletions in Bihar
events.organiser: CPI(ML) Liberation, Bihar State unit
events.place: Patna
events.quote: Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation General Secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya on Thursday (October 1, 2026) slammed the Election Commission of India (ECI) over alleged illegalities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
events.what: A public hearing in Patna where about 20 voters whose names were allegedly deleted gave testimony before a five-member jury. It was based on a voter verification survey the party ran in seven Bihar districts.

events.title: Protest at Shivaji Park
events.organiser: Cockroach Janta Party
events.place: Shivaji Park, Mumbai
events.quote: the group will hold a protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park, a no-sound or silence zone, on Friday (October 2, 2026)
events.what: A protest calling for the Chief Election Commissioner to resign. The police had not granted permission when it was announced.

events.title: 'Save Democracy' marches in all districts
events.organiser: INDIA bloc
events.place: District headquarters across India, ending in demonstrations before district magistrates' offices
events.quote: Under that “save democracy” marches will be taken out in all districts from October 2-8 and demonstrations will be held before the district magistrate’s office, the Congress President stated, adding that youth and NGOs would also be invited for the event.
events.what: The INDIA bloc announced 'save democracy' marches in every district from 2 to 8 October, ending in demonstrations outside district magistrates' offices. Reports show some were held, including a protest by INDIA bloc parties outside the Collectorate in Hyderabad on 6 October and a march by the RJD, Congress and Left in Patna on 7 October.

events.title: Virat Garjana Morcha (Grand Roar March)
events.organiser: Shiv Sena (UBT) and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, with state leaders of the Congress and NCP (SP)
events.place: Metro Cinema to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters, south Mumbai
events.quote: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) boss Raj Thackeray on Sunday (October 4, 2026) led a protest march in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
events.what: A march in Mumbai led by Uddhav Thackeray and Raj Thackeray against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Participants demanded his removal or resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR. Party flags were not allowed and marchers carried the national flag.

events.title: INDIA bloc MPs' march from Parliament to the Election Commission
events.organiser: INDIA bloc (Congress, Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress, CPI(M) and other parties), with BJD leaders
events.place: Parliament House towards Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi
events.quote: The Delhi Police on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) detained around 260 people, including 10 Members of Parliament, during a protest march by the INDIA bloc from Parliament House towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) office.
events.what: Opposition MPs marched from Parliament House towards the Election Commission's headquarters. Police stopped the march at barricades and detained about 260 people, including 10 MPs. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress leaders were detained after they began a sit-in inside the Akashvani Bhawan premises.

events.title: Protest and people's tribunal at Freedom Park
events.organiser: Cockroach Janta Party
events.place: Freedom Park, Bengaluru
events.quote: The Bengaluru protest is scheduled for October 8 at 10:30 am at Freedom Park.
events.what: A protest against the revision with a people's tribunal.

events.title: Lok Bhavan March
events.organiser: INDIA bloc (Mahagathbandhan) in Bihar, led by RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, with the Congress, VIP, CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation and Indian Inclusive Party
events.place: From the Seven Martyrs statue in front of the Bihar Vidhan Sabha towards Lok Bhavan, Patna. Stopped at the third barricade
events.quote: The INDIA bloc (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) leaders, led by Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) National Working President Tejashwi Yadav, on Thursday (October 8, 2026) took out a massive Lok Bhavan March in Patna.
events.what: A march in Patna by INDIA bloc parties towards Lok Bhavan demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police stopped it at the third barricade and detained several leaders. A delegation led by Tejashwi Yadav then gave the Governor of Bihar a memorandum addressed to the President.

events.title: Protest at Jantar Mantar
events.organiser: Cockroach Janta Party
events.place: Jantar Mantar, New Delhi
events.quote: has announced another protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10, 2026
events.what: A protest calling for the Chief Election Commissioner to resign. The disputes page carries the report of the day itself.

events.title: 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' block-level marches
events.organiser: Indian National Congress
events.place: Block level across India, ending at Sub Divisional Magistrates' offices
events.quote: From October 10 to 20, block-level marches will be held, culminating at Sub Divisional Magistrates offices under the ‘Vote bachao, Desh bachao’ umbrella.
events.what: The Congress announced block-level marches from 10 to 20 October, ending at Sub Divisional Magistrates' offices, as part of its 'Vote bachao, Desh bachao' campaign. The campaign also asks the party's booth agents to find voters deleted unfairly and help them re-enrol.

events.title: Left Front protests across West Bengal
events.organiser: Left Front and student organisations of the Left parties
events.place: Across West Bengal (places not specified)
events.quote: The Left Front and student organisations associated with the Left parties staged protests across the State on October 11, demanding the resignation of the CEC and the scrapping of SIR.
events.what: Protests across West Bengal by the Left Front and Left student organisations demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and the scrapping of the SIR.

events.title: March for Democracy
events.organiser: INDIA bloc (Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD, Shiv Sena (UBT), Trinamool Congress, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, CPI and others), with the student bodies AISA, SFI and AISF
events.place: Constitution Club towards the Supreme Court, New Delhi, through central Delhi and back via Mandi House. Stopped by police near the Supreme Court
events.quote: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other leaders from the INDIA bloc during the march from Barakhamba to Supreme Court in New Delhi on October 12, 2026
events.what: A march through central Delhi from the Constitution Club towards the Supreme Court, where Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a petition over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the SIR. Police stopped the procession near the court. The Congress said 2.5 lakh people took part.

events.title: Procession against the CEC and SIR (stopped by police)
events.organiser: Trinamool Congress (the faction led by Mamata Banerjee), with Dola Sen, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay and Kunal Ghosh
events.place: Rajabazar, Kolkata
events.quote: Leaders and supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, who had gathered in Kolkata on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) to hold a procession in protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Special Intensive Revision (SIR), were not allowed to march as the police said that no permission was obtained for the event.
events.what: Leaders and supporters of the Trinamool Congress faction led by Mamata Banerjee gathered at Rajabazar in Kolkata for a procession against the Chief Election Commissioner and the SIR. Police did not allow them to march, saying no permission had been sought, and the crowd dispersed.

events.title: Lok Bhawan March by Left students' and youth wings
events.organiser: Students' and youth wings of Left parties, including AISA and RYA (CPI(ML) Liberation) and the CPI's student wing, with the Bheem Army
events.place: Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan (Lok Bhawan), Patna
events.quote: Young protesters and members of the students’ wings of Left parties, including the Communist Party of India-Marxist-Leninist (CPI-M-L), the Communist Party of India (CPI), the Revolutionary Youth Association (RYA), and the Bheem Army took out a protest march in Patna on Tuesday (October 13, 2026), seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and re-elections in Bihar and West Bengal, where, they alleged “vote chori (theft) through the SIR (Special Intensive Revision)” had taken place.
events.what: Student and youth activists marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan in Patna over the SIR. Police stopped them near Dak Bungalow roundabout and detained many.

events.title: BJP district rallies backing the SIR (statewide mass awareness campaign)
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Assam unit
events.place: District headquarters across Assam. Rallies were reported in Nalbari on 13 October, Guwahati and Jorhat on 14 October, and Silchar
events.quote: The mobilisation followed Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma’s announcement on Monday that the BJP would hold peaceful rallies at district headquarters across Assam from October 13 to 31.
events.what: A series of BJP rallies at district headquarters in Assam backing the Prime Minister and the SIR of electoral rolls. In Guwahati the state party chief Dilip Saikia led a 'Jana Jagaran Samadal' rally from Khanapara.

events.title: Public hearing of the Independent Commission on SIR
events.organiser: Independent Commission on the Special Intensive Revision, chaired by Justice Madan B. Lokur, proposed by the Lawyers' Association for Constitution
events.place: Jawahar Bhawan, Dr Rajendra Prasad Road, Windsor Place, New Delhi
events.quote: Date: Thursday, 15 October 2026
events.what: Voters gave testimony to a panel of retired judges. The release calls it the first of a series of hearings across the country. No later date had been announced by 22 October.

events.title: 'Stop Vote Chori' protest at Parliament Square
events.organiser: Indian Overseas Congress Youth wing, supported by Save Democracy, SFI U.K. and South Asia Solidarity Group
events.place: Mahatma Gandhi statue, Parliament Square, London
events.quote: Hundreds gathered at Mahatma Gandhi’s statue at Parliament Square in London on Saturday (October 17, 2026) for a protest organised by the Opposition Congress and UK-based Indian students’ groups against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
events.what: A protest in London against the Chief Election Commissioner and the SIR, with Dhruv Rathee as keynote speaker. A smaller group of government supporters held a counter-protest nearby.

events.title: Jan Sunwai on a public audit of the roll in Okhla
events.organiser: Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, Voter Adhikar Manch and the National Federation of Indian Women
events.place: Batla House area, Jamia Nagar, Okhla, New Delhi
events.quote: held in the Batla House area of the national capital on Sunday (October 18, 2026)
events.what: A public hearing on a door-to-door audit of the roll in two polling booths. More than 150 voters registered to put their cases to a panel of advocates and activists.

events.title: Uttar Pradesh Congress press conference on Pilibhit Sadar's roll
events.organiser: Indian National Congress (Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee)
events.place: Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters, Lucknow
events.quote: Addressing a press conference at the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee headquarters in Lucknow, AICC in-charge for UP Rajendra Pal Gautam alleged that the Election Commission had created a system through which "anyone can be defeated, and anyone can be made to win".
events.what: Congress leaders alleged that the names of 13,150 voters in Pilibhit Sadar were changed after the final roll while their EPIC numbers stayed the same, and asked for an inquiry.

events.title: 'Save democracy, end mob rule' campaign
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Haryana unit (Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and state president Archana Gupta)
events.place: Across Haryana. Public meetings at district level and foot marches in assembly constituencies
events.quote: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Haryana will launch “save democracy, end mob rule” campaign from October 22 to November 5 to counter opposition political parties’ “repeated attempts” to question the credibility of constitutional institutions and undermine public confidence in the democratic system.
events.what: A 15-day BJP campaign in Haryana of press conferences, foot marches, district public meetings and constituency discussions presenting the party's case on the Election Commission and the SIR.

events.title: People's March to Reclaim Democracy
events.organiser: People Against SIR, an alliance of organisations formed on 14 October 2026
events.place: 87 gatherings in 15 states on the organisers' map, the New Delhi one at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
events.quote: find the one nearest you and bring your friends along.
events.what: Marches and gatherings across the country on one day. The organisers' map lists 87 for 23 October, 26 of them in Karnataka, 12 in Madhya Pradesh and 9 in Rajasthan. Of those, 63 name a place, 74 give a time and 29 name a host. The New Delhi gathering is hosted by Voter Adhikar Manch and five other groups.

events.title: Human chain on Tank Bund
events.organiser: Telangana Voter Rights Forum (student and civil society organisations)
events.place: Tank Bund, along Hussain Sagar, Hyderabad
events.quote: Hundreds of people formed a human chain at Hyderabad’s Tank Bund along Hussain Sagar Lake on Saturday evening, demanding the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the repeal of the CEC Act, 2023.
events.what: Hundreds of people formed a human chain against the revision. They asked for the revision to be scrapped, for the Chief Election Commissioner to be removed and for the CEC Act, 2023 to be repealed. The report says civil society, human rights, farmers', Dalit, youth and student organisations organised it together.

events.title: Gatherings of 24 and 25 October added to the People Against SIR map
events.place: Pune, Ranchi, Jamshedpur, Netarhat, Rewa, Aligarh, Ballia, Lucknow, Chennai (Kilpauk) and Raipur on 24 October, and Pune (Bibwewadi) and Rae Bareli on 25 October
events.quote: Parivartan Chowk to Hazratganj
events.what: Twelve gatherings against the revision that the People Against SIR map lists for 24 and 25 October, besides the Hyderabad and Mumbai gatherings listed separately. Ten are on 24 October and two on 25 October. Seven name a place, seven give a time and four name a host, among them RRR (Resist, Reclaim, Rebuild) Abhiyan in Pune, Voters Rights Network Tamil Nadu in Chennai and India Democracy Forum in Raipur.

events.organiser: MJP and Youth Welfare Telangana
events.place: Dharna Chowk, Indira Park, Hyderabad
events.quote: Dharna Chowk, Indira Park
events.what: A protest against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: Workers' March Against SIR in Govandi
events.organiser: Workers' March Against SIR
events.place: Samvidhan Chowk, Lallubhai Compound, Govandi, Mumbai
events.quote: Samvidhan Chowk, Lallubhai Compound, Govandi
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: 'Loktantra bachao, bheedtantra hatao' campaign in Dakshina Kannada
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Dakshina Kannada unit (district president Satish Kumpala, committee led by Kishore Kumar Puttur, MLC)
events.place: Across Dakshina Kannada. Padayatras at district and Assembly constituency level, and sessions with youth and intellectuals
events.quote: District and Assembly constituency-level padayatras and interactive sessions with youth and intellectuals over SIR will be held as part of the campaign, he said.
events.what: A BJP campaign in Dakshina Kannada, part of the party's national campaign, which the district president said is aimed at public awareness of the revision, the accuracy of the voter lists and constitutional processes. The padayatras are to end by 5 November and the sessions with youth and intellectuals run to 30 November.

events.title: Gathering at Palakkad stadium bus stand
events.organiser: Collective for Democracy, Palakkad
events.place: Stadium Bus Stand, Palakkad
events.quote: Stadium Bus Stand
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.organiser: AIKMS, SKM
events.place: Dhurpur, Uttar Pradesh
events.quote: Dhurpur
events.what: A march against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.place: From Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Bhavan to the Taluk Administrative Complex, H. D. Kote
events.quote: March from Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Bhavan to the Taluk Administrative Complex
events.what: A march against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.organiser: Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, NFIW and Voter Adhikar Manch, as The Indian Express reports
events.place: Trilokpuri Sabji Mandi, East Delhi
events.quote: The audit covered 1,236 voters across 700 households in four polling booths in Trilokpuri
events.what: A public hearing on a four-day door-to-door audit of booths 42, 43, 79 and 80, where the organisers say 416 of the 1,236 electors they verified had been wrongly listed as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate. Rahul Gandhi, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Yogendra Yadav and Prashant Bhushan attended, and The Indian Express describes volunteers helping a resident fill Form 6 there.

events.organiser: Students' and Youth Collective
events.place: Kakkanad, Ernakulam
events.quote: Kakkanad
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: Protest at the Deputy Commissioner's Office, Yadgir
events.place: In front of the Deputy Commissioner's Office, Yadgir
events.quote: In front of the Deputy Commissioner's Office
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Chandni Chowk, Delhi
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (national president Nitin Nabin, with Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra)
events.time: 4:30 pm, as announced the day before
events.place: From Gauri Shankar Temple to Town Hall Chowk, Chandni Chowk, New Delhi
events.quote: march from Gauri Shankar Temple to Town Hall Chowk in Chandni Chowk, in New Delhi, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026
events.what: A BJP foot march in Delhi led by the party's national president. Outlook says it targeted the Congress over its allegations of vote theft and came ahead of the INDIA bloc rally of 1 November, and ANI describes the BJP's marches across the country as its answer to the opposition's 'Vote Chori' campaign.

events.title: INDIA bloc march to the Chief Electoral Officer's office, Agartala
events.organiser: INDIA bloc, Tripura (CPI(M) state secretary Jitendra Chaudhury and Tripura Pradesh Congress president Ashish Kumar Saha)
events.place: From Orient Chowmuhani to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Tripura, Agartala
events.quote: प्रदर्शनकारी अगरतला के ओरिएंट चौमुहानी से सुबह 11 बजे मार्च शुरू कर त्रिपुरा के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी (सीईओ) के कार्यालय पहुंचेंगे और वहां अपनी मांगों को लेकर ज्ञापन सौंपेंगे।
events.what: The INDIA bloc in Tripura announced a march against the revision ending with a memorandum at the Chief Electoral Officer's office. It demands that the revision be cancelled, that the Chief Election Commissioner be taken out of office and that the legal provisions on the Commission's independence be reviewed, and it opposes the provisions that give the Chief Election Commissioner legal protection.

events.organiser: HSRA_2.0
events.place: Shaheed Smarak Park, Agra
events.quote: Shaheed Smarak Park
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: BJP 'Save Democracy' marches in Himachal Pradesh
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Himachal Pradesh unit (state president Rajeev Bindal)
events.place: Dharamshala on 30 October, Shimla on 1 November (from the Old Bus Stand to Chakkar ground, as The News Mill reports), and Mandi and Hamirpur on 4 November
events.quote: The Kangra constituency march will be held in Dharamshala on Oct 30, while Hamirpur and Mandi will host separate marches on Nov 4.
events.what: Four BJP marches, one in each of the state's parliamentary constituencies, which the state president said would set out the party's position on the revision. The Indian Express reports that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma led the Shimla march on 1 November, with Bindal, Anurag Thakur and Suresh Kashyap.

events.title: 'Raise the Flag of Freedom' gathering in Thrissur
events.organiser: A secular democratic collective of cultural activists, human rights defenders and political and social organisations, as The Hindu reports
events.time: 4:00 pm, with the programme until 10:00 pm
events.place: Rally from the CMS School premises to the Kerala Sahitya Akademi, Thrissur, with the programme at the Akademi's Basheer venue
events.quote: will organise a solidarity gathering titled ‘Raise the Flag of Freedom’ on October 30
events.what: A protest rally and an evening of music and other cultural programmes in support of the protests against the revision, with writers, film-makers and musicians expected to take part.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' marches in Rajasthan
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Rajasthan unit (Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma and state president Madan Rathore)
events.place: Kota and Alwar on 30 October, Tijara on 31 October, Udaipur, and Jaipur and Alwar on 5 November (in Jaipur a public meeting at Ramlila Maidan, then a march from Sanganeri Gate to Tripolia Gate)
events.quote: अभियान की शुरुआत 30 अक्टूबर को कोटा से होगी, जहां मुख्यमंत्री भजनलाल शर्मा और प्रदेश अध्यक्ष मदन राठौड़ मोर्चा संभालेंगे.
events.what: The first phase of a BJP campaign of public meetings and foot marches in 15 districts of Rajasthan. The state general secretary said it would make the public aware of the integrity of the roll and the revision. ETV Bharat reports that the party means to answer the questions the Congress raises about the electoral process, and presents the campaign as the BJP's answer to the Congress rally in Delhi on 1 November. Union Ministers Jyotiraditya Scindia, Bhupender Yadav, Krishan Pal Gurjar and Ashwini Vaishnaw are to lead marches in Alwar, Tijara, Udaipur and Jaipur. The party says the remaining districts will follow after Diwali.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' padyatra in Indore
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Indore city unit (city president Sumit Mishra)
events.place: From Subhash Nagar Chauraha to Patnipura Chauraha, Indore, ending in a public meeting at Patnipura
events.quote: यात्रा का मुख्य उद्देश्य एसआईआर प्रक्रिया की वास्तविकता से जनता को अवगत कराना और विपक्ष के नैरेटिव का उत्तर देना है।
events.what: A BJP foot march through Indore, which the organisers said was to tell the public about the revision and answer the opposition. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and state president Hemant Khandelwal were named among those expected to take part. Webdunia reports that the route was barricaded and traffic diverted, that a family taking a child with a fever to hospital said the police stopped them, and that the police detained a social worker who came with a poster.

events.title: 'Democracy vs Anarchy' mock parliament, New Delhi
events.organiser: Citizens for Democracy
events.place: NDMC Convention Centre, New Delhi
events.quote: Citizens for Democracy will organise a mock parliament on the theme ‘Democracy vs Anarchy’ at the NDMC Convention Centre in New Delhi on October 30, beginning at 10:30 am.
events.what: A mock parliament, announced as one in which young people from different parts of the country would take the roles of leaders of the ruling side and the opposition. The announcement listed the revision of the rolls, electronic voting machines, the Election Commission's role, the allegations of vote theft and the recent protests among the subjects to be debated. The Daily Jagran, citing News18, described it as a counter to the INDIA bloc's protest and said no BJP leaders or MPs were taking part. Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal called the groups holding it BJP-sponsored.

events.title: ABVP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Patna
events.organiser: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (national secretary Abhay Pratap Singh, with DUSU president Yash Dabas)
events.place: From Kargil Chowk to Dak Bungalow Chauraha, Patna
events.quote: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members on Friday (October 30, 2026) took out a protest march in Bihar’s Patna under the campaign ‘Loktantra Bachao Arajakta Hatao’ (Save Democracy, End Anarchy).
events.what: A student march in Patna against what the organisers called attempts to weaken democracy and democratic institutions. Abhay Pratap Singh told the gathering that the revision is a regular administrative process and that allegations of irregularities in it should be raised before constitutional forums with evidence. The Hindu reports that marchers crossed police barricades on the way.

events.title: INDIA bloc 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner
events.organiser: INDIA bloc (announced by Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal)
events.place: The lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's official residence, 10 Rajaji Marg, New Delhi
events.quote: The event, originally scheduled for Friday, October 30, will now be held on Saturday, October 31, at the lawns of 10 Rajaji Marg
events.what: A mock Parliament of INDIA bloc MPs and leaders, which the opposition called a 'Jan Mahabhiyog', held on 31 October on the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence after rain put it back by a day. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided and Kharge moved a motion of six charges against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, among them the deletion of 13.2 crore voters through the SIR, the change to Form 6 without Parliament's approval, centralising control of the rolls through the ERONET and ECINET software, and shutting out the other two Election Commissioners. The Hindu reports that the proceedings lasted three and a half hours and that the motion was adopted unanimously by a show of hands. The Wire counted 37 speakers, among them MPs from 18 parties, activists and electors who said their names had been deleted. Rahul Gandhi closed the discussion, called the exercise a 'political weapon' and said Kumar should be removed and tried for treason. It has no legal effect, since a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only by Parliament in the manner of a Supreme Court judge. It came the day before the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November.

events.title: BJP 'Save Democracy, End Autocracy' rally in Agartala
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Tripura unit (state president and MLA Abhishek Debroy)
events.place: Agartala
events.quote: The Tripura unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will hold a rally in Agartala on October 31 under the slogan “Save Democracy, End Autocracy”, accusing Opposition parties of misleading people through rumours and provocation.
events.what: A BJP rally in Agartala that the party called an answer to the opposition's criticism of the revision. India Today NE reports that the rally would also put forward the BJP's support for the revision, and Debroy defended the revision as an exercise carried out under earlier governments. Tripura's own revision has been put back to begin in December. The INDIA bloc held a protest in Agartala the day before.

events.title: INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, hosting INDIA bloc parties, with student bodies and civil society organisations
events.place: Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi
events.quote: The Delhi Police has issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) allowing the Congress to hold a one-day rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on November 1, a senior police officer said on Saturday.
events.what: A one-day rally in Delhi organised by the Congress as part of the INDIA bloc's campaign against the SIR. Delhi Police issued a no-objection certificate. Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal said on 24 October that a 'Dilli Chalo March' would end at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November, and Mahila Congress chief Alka Lamba said the rally would not be postponed or cancelled. Rahul Gandhi called it the 'Vote Bachao Desh Bachao Jan March and Maharally' in a post on X on 25 October, and on 31 October gave the march's route from the Connaught Place and Minto Road junction by Ajmeri Gate to Ramlila Maidan, starting at noon. Delhi Traffic Police announced restrictions in central Delhi from 10 am to 5 pm on 1 November. Delhi Police sources told ANI on 31 October that no permission had been sought for a march from Connaught Place. On 1 November senior leaders, among them Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, M. A. Baby, D. Raja and Dipankar Bhattacharya, left Kharge's residence for Minto Road in an open bus to march to Ramlila Maidan, The Hindu reported. The Indian Express reported that Delhi Police put the ground's working capacity at 30,000 to 40,000 people while the organisers expected up to 10 lakh. Rahul Gandhi alleged on X that the BJP had forcibly shut every shop at Connaught Place. The march and rally went ahead on 1 November. The Hindu reported that leaders including Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, M. A. Baby, D. Raja, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Sanjay Raut and Supriya Sule attended, and The Hindu and The Wire report speeches by Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav. Scroll reported that the Chief Ministers of Telangana, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh joined. The Wire reported that the Aam Aadmi Party and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, which it says are no longer in the INDIA bloc, stayed away, and that the Cockroach Janta Party, which had pledged its support, was absent. Scroll put the crowd at tens of thousands and The Wire at thousands. BJP MP Sambit Patra said about 40% of the ground was empty, and K. C. Venugopal said on X that Delhi had never seen an uprising on this scale, without giving a number. Rahul Gandhi said in his speech that Gyanesh Kumar would be removed as Chief Election Commissioner and would go to jail, and that legal action would follow against Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Kharge said the bloc would keep fighting until Kumar goes. None of the reports read gives a resolution adopted at the rally.

events.title: Meeting in Vijayawada
events.organiser: "Wake Up, Andhra Pradesh" Allied Organizations
events.place: Makineni Basavapunnaiah Vignana Kendram, near Raghavaiah Park, Vijayawada
events.quote: Makineni Basavapunnaiah Vignana Kendram (MBVK), near Raghavaiah Park
events.what: A gathering against the revision, listed on the People Against SIR map.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' padyatras in Rohtak and Faridabad
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (national president Nitin Nabin in Rohtak, and Dharmendra Pradhan in Faridabad)
events.place: From Chhotu Ram Polytechnic Ground to D-Park, Model Town, Rohtak, and from B.K. Chowk, NIT, Faridabad
events.quote: Mr. Nabin’s padyatra will begin from Chhotu Ram Polytechnic Ground and culminate at D-Park in Model Town, where Mr. Nabin will also pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at his statue, the BJP said in a statement.
events.what: BJP foot marches in Haryana on the day of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. PTI reports that the party set them against what it called the opposition's 'misinformation, propaganda and orchestrated chaos', and describes the INDIA bloc rally as one against the SIR and alleged vote theft. The Indian Express reports that the Rohtak march ended at D-Park, where Nabin paid tribute at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi, and that Pradhan spoke to reporters in Faridabad.

events.title: AAP 'Tiranga Yatra' in Rohtak
events.organiser: Aam Aadmi Party, Haryana unit (state president Sushil Gupta)
events.place: From Mansarovar Park to Ambedkar Chowk, Rohtak
events.quote: The AAP leader said the party would organise a ‘Tiranga Yatra’ in Rohtak on November 1 to protest against what it termed vote theft and demand the CEC’s resignation.
events.what: An AAP march in Rohtak on Haryana Day, announced by the party's state president against what the party calls vote theft and for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner. Gupta said the party had parted ways with the INDIA bloc, and the march fell on the day of the bloc's rally in Delhi. Gupta put the votes deleted at 34 lakh in Haryana and 47 lakh in Delhi. The names left off the two states' draft rolls in the revision were 33.8 lakh and 47.6 lakh. He said the party had told the district administration and the police about the march in writing a month in advance.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Delhi on 1 November
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra)
events.place: Delhi (route not stated)
events.quote: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta joined Delhi BJP Chief Harsh Malhotra and senior party leaders in leading the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march through the capital.
events.what: A BJP march in Delhi on the day of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, under the name of the party's campaign of marches. The Indian Express reports that the leaders wore black headbands for the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, in protest against the Congress holding its rally on the anniversary. The Wire reports that the march was held to mark the anniversary of the riots.

events.title: March from Ramlila Maidan towards Jantar Mantar
events.organiser: Disha Students' Organisation and Revolutionary Workers' Party of India
events.place: From Ramlila Maidan towards Jantar Mantar, stopped at Minto Road, New Delhi
events.quote: Police said the rally was taken out by members of the Disha Students’ Organisation and the Revolutionary Workers’ Party of India (RWPI) on Sunday around 5 pm.
events.what: A march by two organisations after the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. A member of the Revolutionary Workers' Party of India said it demanded that Jantar Mantar be reclaimed as a protest site and that the SIR be scrapped. Police stopped it at Minto Road and registered an FIR against 22 of those they detained.

events.title: BJP padayatra in Hyderabad ('Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao')
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Telangana unit (state president N. Ramchander Rao)
events.place: From the Babu Jagjivan Ram statue near Nizam College in Fateh Maidan to a public meeting at MJ Market, Hyderabad
events.quote: Amit Shah ji will attend the padayatra on the 2nd (of November)
events.what: A BJP foot march in Hyderabad which the state party president, N. Ramchander Rao, said was meant to answer what he called the Congress's false narrative on the revision. Union Home Minister Amit Shah led it on 2 November with Rao, the Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy and the Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, from the Babu Jagjivan Ram statue near Nizam College to a public meeting at MJ Market in the Old City, The Hindu reported. At the meeting Shah said the Union government was ready to convene a special session of Parliament and challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate the revision there, The Hindu and PTI reported.

events.title: BJP press conference on the SIR in Varanasi
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (MP and spokesperson Sambit Patra)
events.place: Circuit House, Varanasi
events.quote: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is aimed at refining voter lists, not “stealing 13 crore votes,” BJP spokesperson and MP Sambit Patra said on Monday
events.what: A press conference by the BJP MP Sambit Patra, a day after the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, at which he replied to Rahul Gandhi's charges against the Election Commission. He said the removal of names was part of verifying and updating the rolls, that the revision identified electors who were absent, had shifted permanently, had died or were entered twice, and that parties could use their booth level agents to find errors in the rolls.

events.title: BJP 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' padyatras in Uttar Pradesh
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Uttar Pradesh unit (campaign convener and state general secretary Dilip Patel)
events.place: Lucknow on 3 November, Prayagraj, Gorakhpur and Kanpur on 4 November, and Ghaziabad and Bareilly on 5 November
events.quote: पार्टी प्रदेश के सभी छह संगठनात्मक क्षेत्रों में तीन से पांच नवंबर तक लोकतंत्र बचाओ-अराजकता हटाओ अभियान के तहत पदयात्राएं निकालेगी।
events.what: BJP foot marches in each of the party's six organisational regions of Uttar Pradesh under the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign. Amar Ujala says they are to answer the opposition's protests and the questions it raises about the electoral process. NDTV reports the campaign's foot marches across the country as the BJP's answer to the INDIA bloc rally of 1 November on the revision, and names a march in Lucknow.

events.title: BJP 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' march in Giridih
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (Jharkhand BJP president Aditya Sahu)
events.place: Jhanda Maidan to Tower Chowk, Giridih
events.quote: In Giridih, hundreds of BJP leaders and workers participated in a 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' march led by state BJP president Aditya Sahu.
events.what: A BJP march of about 300 metres in Giridih under the name of the party's campaign of marches, with the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, Babulal Marandi, and the former state BJP president Ravindra Rai. Marandi said the Congress and the INDIA bloc had tried to mislead people since 2014, first over EVMs and now over the SIR.

events.title: ABVP march in Ranchi
events.organiser: Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, Jharkhand unit
events.place: Bapu Vatika to Albert Ekka Chowk, Ranchi
events.quote: Meanwhile, the Jharkhand unit of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) also took out a march in Ranchi, asserting that political disagreements should be addressed through constitutional means rather than street protests.
events.what: A march by the ABVP's Jharkhand unit, which said political disagreements should be taken up through constitutional means and that transparency in the voter list is needed. A member of its central working committee said the Congress had spread confusion about the SIR.

events.title: Rail roko in Kanchipuram demanding the arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner
events.organiser: Jananayaka Meetpu Kuzhu, with members of Makkal Mandram, the Communist Party of India and the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi
events.place: From near Hotel Tamil Nadu to the East Railway Station, Kanchipuram
events.quote: Tension prevailed near the old railway station in Kanchipuram on Wednesday after members of the Jananayaka Meetpu Kuzhu staged a rail roko protest demanding the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
events.what: More than 350 people marched to the station and more than 50 sat on the tracks, demanding the arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner. Police detained all of them.

events.title: INDIA bloc protest against SIR at Freedom Park, Bengaluru
events.organiser: INDIA bloc Karnataka unit (KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad), with Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Samajwadi Party and Forward Bloc
events.place: Freedom Park, Bengaluru
events.quote: In continuation of this, the INDIA bloc has assembled today at Freedom Park, and we are going to start our protest today.
events.what: A protest against the revision by INDIA bloc parties in Karnataka, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The KPCC president, B.K. Hariprasad, said District Congress Committee presidents were holding rallies at the district headquarters the same day and that the protest would go on until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned.

events.title: BJP padayatra in Karnal with Amit Shah
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Haryana unit (state president Archana Gupta)
events.place: From Sector 12 to Dayanand Chowk, Karnal
events.quote: The Home Minister on Thursday led the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march from Sector 12 to the Dayanand Chowk in Karnal.
events.what: A BJP foot march in Karnal led by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Union Minister Manohar Lal, the state BJP president Archana Gupta and the party's Haryana in-charge Smriti Irani. At a rally after the march Shah repeated his proposal of a special session of Parliament to discuss the SIR. It fell on the last day of the Haryana campaign in ev-26.

events.title: BJP 'Save Democracy, End Anarchy' march in Shivamogga
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Shivamogga (district president N.K. Jagadish)
events.place: From Ramanna Shreshthi Park to Allama Prabhu Park, Shivamogga
events.quote: BJP leaders and workers taking out a protest march in Shivamogga under the slogan ‘Save Democracy, End Anarchy’ on Thursday.
events.what: A BJP march against the parties opposing the revision, led by the Union Minister Shobha Karandlaje, the former Minister Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri, the MLC C.T. Ravi and the Shivamogga MP B.Y. Raghavendra, with a meeting at Allama Prabhu Park after it.

events.title: BJP march and public meeting on the SIR in Malappuram
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Malappuram (State vice-president V. Unnikrishnan inaugurated the planning meeting)
events.place: Malappuram (route and venue not stated)
events.quote: The BJP will organise a march here on November 6 to counter what it calls misinformation about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
events.what: A BJP march in Malappuram followed by a public meeting, which the party says is part of its nationwide campaign to explain the need for the revision.

events.title: 'Jantar Mantar at Kochi' march and meeting against the SIR
events.organiser: Cockroach Janta Party
events.place: From Marine Drive to Rajendra Maidan, Kochi
events.quote: The demonstration, organised at Rajendra Maidan, demanded the withdrawal of the SIR and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
events.what: The actor Prakash Raj led a march from Marine Drive to a meeting at Rajendra Maidan, where the group's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, spoke. The protest called for the revision to be withdrawn and the Chief Election Commissioner to resign. The organisers put the march at about 500, and the state president of the DYFI, Chintha Jerome, took part.

events.title: Congress village chaupals at which deleted names are to be read out, until 15 December
events.organiser: Indian National Congress (announced by general secretary (organisation) K. C. Venugopal)
events.place: Villages across the country
events.quote: As part of the 'Vote Rakshak' campaign, Venugopal said, village 'chaupals' will be held across India by December 15, where deleted names will be read out.
events.what: Village meetings that the Congress has asked its grassroots units to hold across the country by 15 December, at which the names of deleted electors are to be read out. They are part of the party's 'Vote Rakshak' campaign within its 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' campaign, under which party workers are to visit every booth to find deleted electors. K. C. Venugopal announced them after reviewing the campaign on 13 November with the party's state in-charges and state presidents. The party has also opened a website, iamvoterakshak.in, on which it says people can check whether their names were deleted, register a protest and apply to be added again.

events.title: Congress 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' chaupal in Tauru
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, Haryana (organised by a party youth leader and attended by the state in-charge Sanjay Dutt and the state president Rao Narender Singh)
events.place: Tauru
events.quote: Congress held a ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ chaupal in Tauru on Monday against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
events.what: A village meeting the Congress held in Tauru against the revision, under its 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' campaign. It was attended by the party's Haryana in-charge Sanjay Dutt, the state president Rao Narender Singh, the AICC observer Rohit Chaudhary, the Rohtak MLA Bharat Bhushan Batra, who is also the party's Gurgaon district observer, and the Gurgaon rural district president Vardhan Yadav. Chaudhary asked party workers to visit households and tell people of their voting rights. The organiser asked that the Election Commission work independently of political interference and ensure a free, fair and transparent election.

events.title: BJP 'Save Democracy, Eradicate Anarchy' padayatra in Diglipur
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, Andaman and Nicobar Islands unit (state president Anil Kumar Tiwari, with the party's national secretary and in-charge for the islands, Jai Prakash)
events.place: From the BJP office in Diglipur to New Durga Market, Diglipur
events.quote: The BJP, Andaman & Nicobar Islands on Tuesday took out a ‘Save Democracy, Eradicate Anarchy’ padayatra at Diglipur District, accusing the Congress of “politicising the SIR of electoral rolls and misleading youngsters to provoke confrontation.”
events.what: A BJP foot march from the party's office in Diglipur to New Durga Market, followed by a public meeting near the market, at which the party accused the Congress of politicising the revision. The Andaman Chronicle reports that more than 1500 people took part and that the march is part of the BJP's campaign across the country to counter the INDIA bloc's narrative against the government at the Centre. Jai Prakash told the meeting that the Congress had no faith in the SIR process, and Anil Kumar Tiwari said the Congress was opposing the revision although voter list revisions had been carried out several times across the country.

events.title: Mahila Congress 'Keralam Jantar Mantar' protest at Lok Bhavan, Thiruvananthapuram
events.organiser: Mahila Congress, Kerala unit (state president Jebi Mather), inaugurated by the AICC general secretary Deepa Dasmunsi
events.place: In front of Keralam Lok Bhavan, Thiruvananthapuram
events.quote: The Mahila Congress on Saturday staged a protest in front of Keralam Lok Bhavan here, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the withdrawal of the SIR of electoral rolls.
events.what: A protest by the Mahila Congress in front of Lok Bhavan in Thiruvananthapuram, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner and the withdrawal of the revision. Deepa Dasmunsi inaugurated it and told hundreds of Mahila Congress workers that the Congress would continue its nationwide protests until the Chief Election Commissioner resigned. Jebi Mather, the UDF convenor and MP Adoor Prakash and the Cultural Affairs Minister P C Vishnunadh also spoke. The protesters carried effigies of the Chief Election Commissioner.

events.title: People's Convention on 'SIR and the Challenges to Constitutional Democracy' in Hyderabad
events.organiser: Forum for Constitutional Democracy (convenor K. Ramachandra Murthy)
events.place: Institution of Engineers (India), Khairatabad, Hyderabad
events.quote: Titled ‘SIR and the Challenges to Constitutional Democracy’, the convention is being organised by the Forum for Constitutional Democracy (FCD) at the Institution of Engineers (India), Khairatabad, at 4 pm.
events.what: A public convention on the revision that the Forum for Constitutional Democracy announced at a press conference at the Press Club in Basheerbagh on 19 November, to be addressed by the Supreme Court advocate Prashant Bhushan. The senior advocate G. Jyothy Kiran said it would be the forum's first public meeting since its formation. At the press conference K. Ramachandra Murthy questioned the credibility of elections when the rolls themselves are in question, and Justice B. Sudershan Reddy called the revision arbitrary and questioned its legal and constitutional basis. Justice Reddy alleged that one person had filed Form 7 applications against hundreds of voters, and referred to cases registered in Telangana and Karnataka over such applications. Prof. Kodandaram raised the deletion and alteration of voters' names and said the scale of the revision called for wider public discussion, and that around 50 intellectuals had come together in the forum. The forum invited citizens, civil society organisations and democratic rights activists to attend.

events.title: Press conference and vigil of transgender and gender-diverse persons on the revision, Press Club of India
events.organiser: An alliance of transgender and gender-diverse persons, which the report does not name
events.place: Press Club of India, New Delhi
events.quote: At a press conference and community vigil at the Press Club of India, New Delhi, on Sunday, an alliance of transgender and gender-diverse persons flagged the exclusion of transgender identity cards from the Election Commission's list of 12 accepted documents.
events.what: A press conference and community vigil on Transgender Day of Remembrance, at which an alliance of transgender and gender-diverse persons pointed to the exclusion of transgender identity cards from the Election Commission's list of 12 accepted documents, The Tribune reported. On the figures the alliance presented, registered transgender electors in 12 states and union territories fell from 35,870 to 24,811 during the revision, a fall of 30.8 per cent and more than 2.5 times the fall in electors overall. The groups argued that a revision relying heavily on documents held by families falls disproportionately on transgender persons estranged from their families or forced to leave home, and that changes of name and address make it harder for them to show they are eligible. The transparency activist Anjali Bhardwaj said that women and transgender persons often face hurdles over documents because of changes of name and address and estrangement from their families, and asked whether a change of address should cost a citizen the vote.

events.title: BJP 'Let Us Protect Democracy, Bury Anarchy' Maha Padayatra in Karimnagar with Nitin Nabin
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party (national president Nitin Nabin, with the Union Minister of State for Home Affairs and Karimnagar MP Bandi Sanjay Kumar)
events.place: Karimnagar
events.quote: BJP President Nitin Nabin would lead a rally on Monday to counter criticism against the SIR exercise and "vote chori" (vote theft) allegations in Telangana's Karimnagar, Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar said.
events.what: A BJP rally in Karimnagar to be led by the party's national president Nitin Nabin, which Bandi Sanjay Kumar said on 22 November would counter criticism of the revision and the allegations of vote theft made against the party. He said the rally would be historic, with a massive turnout of BJP activists and people. The Hindu calls it the party's 'Let Us Protect Democracy, Bury Anarchy' Maha Padayatra and reports that leaders expect more than one lakh people to take part.

events.title: Press conference in Mumbai announcing the second phase of the campaign against the revision
events.organiser: PUCL, APCR and Maharashtra SIR Jagruti Abhiyan, as the People Against SIR listing gives the hosts
events.place: Mumbai
events.quote: The second phase of the campaign to scrap the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls will begin on Thursday, November 26, observed as Constitution Day, with a focus on Maharashtra and other states where the revision process is still incomplete, activists associated with the nationwide protests announced in Mumbai on Tuesday.
events.what: A press conference in Mumbai at which activists associated with the nationwide protests announced that the second phase of the campaign against the revision would begin on Constitution Day, 26 November, with a focus on Maharashtra and other states where the revision is still incomplete, the Free Press Journal reported. Representatives of the Association for Protection of Civil Rights, the People's Union for Civil Liberties, the Maharashtra SIR Janajagruti Abhiyan and the Cockroach Janta Party called for the revision to be cancelled and said the Commission had no documents to show that it had itself taken the decision to conduct it. Anjali Bhardwaj of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information, the senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, Yogendra Yadav of the Bharat Jodo Abhiyan and the advocate Mihir Desai of the PUCL spoke. The paper notes that the Supreme Court upheld the Commission's authority to conduct the revision in its judgment of 27 May 2026 on Bihar.

events.title: Rally on Anna Salai, Chennai, against the SIR
events.organiser: Independent Young Citizens Collective, part of People Against SIR
events.place: Anna Salai, Chennai
events.quote: Announcing a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the collective said the reported deletion of such a large number of names has raised serious questions about the exercise and its implications for democracy.
events.what: A rally that the collective announced at a press conference at the Chennai Press Club on 10 November, as part of what it called a nationwide day of action against the revision. The political economist Parakala Prabhakar, the Carnatic vocalist T.M. Krishna, Thomas Franco, a former General Secretary of the All India Bank Officers' Confederation, and the collective's co-convenor Radhika Ganesh spoke at the press conference. The collective demanded an inquiry into the fall in Tamil Nadu's roll, which it put at 74.07 lakh names. Prabhakar called for the revision to be scrapped and for every eligible voter whose name was deleted to be restored.

events.title: Protests across the country called by People Against SIR, 26 November to 20 December
events.organiser: People Against SIR, a platform of civil society, student and farmers' organisations
events.place: Across the country, beginning with demonstrations on Constitution Day, 26 November
events.quote: People Against SIR (PA-SIR), a platform for civil society, students and farmers’ organisations, has decided to step up its agitation against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, giving a call for peaceful protests across the country between November 26 and December 20.
events.what: People Against SIR has called for peaceful protests against the revision between 26 November and 20 December, The Hindu reported. The call was decided by the platform's National Coordination Committee and planned at a meeting of its working group on 12 November. According to the report, the groups would mark Constitution Day on 26 November with demonstrations across the country to assert the 'Right to Vote, Right to Livelihood', and would hold public meetings and rallies and audit voter lists until 20 December. The agitation would also include dharnas, a People's Parliament and a people's referendum. In a statement after the meeting the platform called the Commission's recent changes belated half measures that leave the mass disenfranchisement unaddressed. The actor Prakash Raj, who is part of the platform, spoke to the press, and the transparency activist Anjali Bhardwaj said the agitation would continue until the revision is scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner is removed and prosecuted. No place or date for a single event after 26 November was given.

events.title: Congress 'Samvidhan Raksha March' by state units on Constitution Day
events.organiser: Indian National Congress (its state units)
events.place: Across the country, organised by the party's state units
events.quote: On November 26, which is the Constitution Day, state units have been tasked to organise 'Samvidhan Raksha March' (march to save Constitution).
events.what: Marches that the Congress's state units have been tasked to hold on Constitution Day, 26 November, as Deccan Herald reported in its account of the party's 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' campaign. The report gives them beside the village chaupals that K. C. Venugopal, the party's general secretary (organisation), announced after reviewing the campaign on 13 November with the party's state in-charges and state presidents.

events.title: Uttar Pradesh Congress 'Samvidhan Bachao Sankalp Yatra' on Constitution Day
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, Uttar Pradesh unit (state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam and state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona')
events.place: Lucknow, from the Congress office towards Ambedkar Crossing in Hazratganj, with foot marches across Uttar Pradesh
events.quote: कांग्रेस कार्यालय से डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर की प्रतिमा तक मार्च निकाला जाएगा।
events.what: A march on Constitution Day from the Congress office to the statue of B. R. Ambedkar, which Rajendra Pal Gautam said would raise questions about the Constitution, democratic rights and the voter list, with foot marches across the state on the same day. Gautam and Aradhana Mishra announced it at a joint press conference at the party's state headquarters in Lucknow, with a campaign in which party workers are to check the voter list of every Assembly constituency in the state. At the press conference the two leaders claimed that 15 per cent more women's votes than men's had been deleted in the revision. The march went ahead on 26 November without permission, PTI and Hindustan Times reported, and PTI reported that the administration had denied it. PTI reported that the party's workers marched from the Congress office in Lucknow towards Ambedkar Crossing in Hazratganj, and that police stopped them about 150 metres from the office at three layers of barricades. After about 40 minutes the police detained Gautam, Mishra, the state unit's working president, Imran Masood, and several other leaders and workers, took them to Eco Garden, which PTI calls the designated protest site in Lucknow, and released them. PTI reported that the Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge attended a 'Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan' at the party office earlier in the day and left for Delhi before the march began. Both reports call the march a 'Samvidhan Raksha' march.

events.title: Haryana Congress 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Panchkula on Constitution Day
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, Haryana unit (state president Rao Narender Singh and the AICC in-charge for Haryana Sanjay Dutt)
events.place: Panchkula
events.quote: The party will also hold a “Save the Constitution March” in Panchkula on November 26 as part of its efforts to mobilise public support on voter rights and constitutional safeguards.
events.what: A march in Panchkula on Constitution Day that the Haryana Congress announced on 17 November, after a meeting at Jat Bhawan in Karnal of its district presidents, the state presidents of its wings and other office-bearers. Sanjay Dutt said senior party leaders, MPs, MLAs, former MLAs, district and block office-bearers, representatives of frontal organisations and citizens were expected to take part. He said the march is part of the party's nationwide initiative under which state units have been asked to organise Constitution Day marches in their states. The party also announced a 'Vote Rakshak' drive from 22 to 30 November, in which Rao Narender Singh said it would deploy at least one trained volunteer at every polling booth to identify voters whose names have been removed from the rolls and verify the circumstances of the deletions.

events.title: BJP rally in Kolkata on Constitution Day to answer the opposition on the revision
events.organiser: Bharatiya Janata Party, West Bengal unit
events.place: Kolkata, with processions in districts across the state
events.quote: 26 नवंबर को संविधान दिवस के अवसर पर कोलकाता में विशाल रैली निकालने का निर्णय लिया गया है।
events.what: A large rally in Kolkata on Constitution Day that the BJP has decided to hold to answer the opposition's attacks on the revision, Dainik Jagran reported, with processions in districts across the state. The paper reports that the party aims to reject the opposition's allegation that the Election Commission has been removing electors' names from the rolls at the BJP's behest, and that the party calls the allegations false. It reports, citing sources, that the party is also considering going door to door.

events.title: Madhya Pradesh Congress 'Samvidhan Raksha March' in Bhopal on Constitution Day
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, Madhya Pradesh unit (Mohammad Arif Naseem Khan, a special invitee to the Congress Working Committee, spoke for it)
events.place: Bhopal
events.quote: The Congress on Thursday said it will hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’ in Madhya Pradesh capital Bhopal on November 26 to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
events.what: A march in Bhopal on Constitution Day that the Congress announced on 19 November against what it alleges are irregularities in the revision. Mohammad Arif Naseem Khan, a special invitee to the Congress Working Committee, said after a meeting in Indore on the preparations that at least 1,000 party workers from each of the state's 230 Assembly constituencies would march to the capital. He alleged that the names of eligible voters are being deleted under the revision at the behest of the BJP. He said the party is also running a 'vote rakshak' campaign in the state, in which its workers go door to door to verify the names of voters who are no longer on the rolls.

events.title: March from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, on Constitution Day
events.organiser: SKM, AIKS, AISA, SFI, DYFI and Collective, as the People Against SIR listing gives the hosts
events.place: Mandir Marg, New Delhi
events.quote: No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, scheduled for November 26, a senior New Delhi police officer told The Hindu.
events.what: A march against the revision on Constitution Day that the People Against SIR map lists at Mandir Marg, New Delhi, at 12:30 pm, with SKM, AIKS, AISA, SFI, DYFI and Collective as hosts. A senior New Delhi police officer told The Hindu that no permission had been sought from the Delhi Police for the march, and the organisers have maintained that they informed the police of it, the paper reported. The paper's standfirst says that People Against SIR, which it describes as a collective of about 200 organisations, has informed the Delhi Police of the march, from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar. On the night of 25 November the New Delhi police posted a notice saying it had received no application for a march by the SKM and other activists from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar and had granted no permission, and that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force in the New Delhi district, The Wire and The Times of India reported. On 26 November the Delhi Police stopped the farmers' march at Mandir Marg, and the farmer leaders Yudhvir Singh and Revula Venkaiah handed a memorandum addressed to the President to an Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, PTI reported from a statement of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha. PTI reported that the Students' Federation of India held a separate march at Mandir Marg against the Chief Election Commissioner over the revision.

events.title: Memoranda to the President in every district of Madhya Pradesh on Constitution Day, decided by organisations of People Against SIR
events.organiser: Organisations linked to People Against SIR in Madhya Pradesh, as the report describes them
events.place: Every district of Madhya Pradesh, through the Collectors, and the Chief Electoral Officer in Bhopal
events.quote: बैठक में प्रदेश के सभी जिलों में 26 नवंबर संविधान दिवस के अवसर पर राष्ट्रपति के नाम ज्ञापन देने का निर्णय लिया गया।
events.what: A meeting of organisations linked to People Against SIR in Madhya Pradesh decided to hand memoranda addressed to the President in every district of the state on Constitution Day, 26 November, through the District Collectors, and to give a memorandum to the state's Chief Electoral Officer in Bhopal the same day seeking the revision's cancellation, according to an unsigned text datelined Bhopal that two news sites carried word for word. The report says members would hand over the memoranda by joining protests organised by the Samyukta Kisan Morcha, and that each programme would open with a reading of the Preamble and close with the burning of copies of the revision's notification. It says the demands of the platform, which it says 150 organisations across the country formed, include cancelling the revision, updating the 2024 roll and the resignation and arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner. It also reports decisions to hold a people's parliament on 10 December at Jantar Mantar seeking its renotification as a site for peaceful protest, people's courts at every polling station on 20 December and a people's parade on Republic Day, 26 January 2027, and to form a state committee soon.

In his post announcing it, Nitin Sethi said they would talk about what the Collective has learnt from more than a year of investigation that has so far produced nearly 50 reports, and invited anyone interested to join.

events.what: A large rally of the INDIA bloc proposed for Bhopal on 12 December, against what the parties allege are irregularities in the revision, Dainik Jagran reported. The paper reports that a meeting in Delhi on 19 November decided to take the agitation from Delhi to the capitals of the states, beginning with Bhopal, and to hold a 'vote rakshak' march as well. It reports that the Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, the MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and the Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav are to attend with senior leaders of other parties. Jitu Patwari confirmed the rally and said leaders of all the alliance's parties would take part and that more than one lakh people would gather.

events.title: INDIA bloc rally in Ahmedabad against the revision
events.organiser: The INDIA bloc of opposition parties
events.place: Ahmedabad
events.quote: The Bhopal rally is scheduled for December 12 while the one in Ahmedabad will be held on December 19.
events.what: A rally of the INDIA bloc in Ahmedabad on 19 December against the revision and the Chief Election Commissioner, after the bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on 1 November and the one planned in Bhopal on 12 December, Deccan Herald reported. The paper reports that the parties are to hold a rally in Kolkata, which it says is likely only after 15 January 2027, and that, according to sources, the bloc is choosing states ruled by the BJP for its protests. The Hindu reported the same day that the bloc plans rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata over the next month.
